title: Gerunds, Infinitives, Participles and Non-Finite Clauses
orientation: A verb can organise a clause without carrying its own tense. In We hope to finish, hope is finite while to finish supplies a second situation whose interpretation depends on the surrounding sentence. These compact structures appear in instructions, academic reporting, everyday plans and formal editing. Today you will identify the different non-finite forms before examining which verbs select them and how their meanings differ. You will then practise shortening clauses without losing agents, time relationships or qualifications. Earlier work on verb phrases, passives and clause structure provides the prerequisites. The expert layer asks who is understood to perform an infinitive and distinguishes control from raising. Those analytical labels explain selected patterns; they are not a reason to force every unusual sentence into one template. Original writing tasks remain self-reviewed against explicit grammatical and meaning criteria.
outcomes: Identify -ing, to-infinitival, bare-infinitival and past-participial forms in context.
Build active, passive and perfect non-finite verb phrases without confusing form with time.
Explain meaning changes after verbs such as remember, stop and try.
Revise purpose and participial clauses while preserving their intended subject.
Use basic control/raising diagnostics while recognising theory-dependent terminology.

modules.title: Non-finite forms and grammatical functions
modules.definition: A non-finite verb form lacks the ordinary independent tense/person agreement contrasts of a finite verb. Non-finite clauses may nevertheless express complex time, aspect, voice and participant relationships through their form and larger context.
foundation: Begin with four useful shapes: to write, write after an appropriate selecting expression, writing and written. In The clerk hopes to write, hopes is the finite verb and to write is an infinitival complement. In The clerk may write, may is finite and write is the following plain form. In The clerk is writing, is is finite and writing is a participial form. Written combines with have in a perfect or be in a passive: has written; was written. The spelling alone is not a complete analysis, because many past-tense and participial forms are identical, as in checked.
intermediate: An -ing clause can fill several functions: Reading the instructions carefully takes time has a subject clause; She enjoys reading the instructions has a complement; Reading the instructions carefully, she noticed an exception has an adjunct. Traditional teaching often calls the first two gerunds and the last a participle. Some modern grammars use the combined label gerund-participial for the verbal form. Neither terminology makes every -ing word a verb. In the careful reading of the instructions, reading is a noun with a determiner and adjective; in reading the instructions carefully, the verb takes a direct object and adverb.
advanced: Build longer forms by applying ordinary auxiliary selection. To have written is a perfect infinitive; to be written is passive; to have been written combines perfect and passive. Having written is a perfect -ing form, and having been written is perfect passive. These forms have no independently inflected tense, but the perfect commonly locates a situation before a contextual reference point. The committee claims to have checked the files attributes the earlier checking as a claim rather than independently guaranteeing its truth. A negative can precede the non-finite phrase: not to sign; not having signed.

A split infinitive places an intervening expression between infinitival to and the plain verb: to carefully compare the estimates. This is a grammatical option in contemporary standard English, not an automatic error. Adverb placement can affect attachment and emphasis. In The team decided to immediately suspend the trial, immediately clearly modifies suspend; The team immediately decided to suspend the trial can instead locate the decision. Do not move an adverb merely to obey an absolute prohibition if that move changes the intended meaning. Some editors prefer an unsplit form where it is equally clear and natural. Follow a specified house style where necessary, while distinguishing its preference from a universal rule of grammar.
expert: Present participle and past participle are traditional form names, not automatic time labels. The files being checked tomorrow refers to future checking even though being is an -ing form; the files checked yesterday has past time because the context supplies it. A non-finite clause may contain auxiliaries, an object and other dependants; it is not merely a loose phrase with no internal syntax. Conversely, a plain verb form does not prove non-finiteness in every context: an imperative such as Write clearly is a main-clause construction. Determine the clause type and selecting environment before assigning a form or function label.

patterns.form: to + have + been + lexical past participle
patterns.meaning: A perfect passive infinitive; the larger context supplies the reference point.
A verbal -ing clause can retain ordinary verb complementation and modification.

examples.sentence: The researcher plans to interview the witnesses.
examples.analysis: Plans is finite; to interview the witnesses is an infinitival complement.

examples.sentence: Carefully checking the figures revealed a discrepancy.
examples.analysis: The whole -ing clause functions as subject; checking takes figures as object and carefully as modifier.

examples.sentence: The letters are believed to have been destroyed.
examples.analysis: The perfect passive infinitive presents destruction as earlier than the attributed belief; the belief is reported, not proved.

contrasts.a: The careful reading of the report took an hour.
contrasts.b: Reading the report carefully took an hour.
contrasts.note: Both are grammatical. The first has a noun reading with adjective careful; the second has a verbal -ing clause with object and adverb.

contrasts.a: The team decided to immediately suspend the trial.
contrasts.b: The team immediately decided to suspend the trial.
contrasts.note: Both can be grammatical. The split version clearly attaches immediately to suspension; the second can place immediacy on deciding. Choose a form that preserves the intended timing.

exceptions: Traditional gerund/participle labels and modern gerund-participial terminology analyse the same many verbal forms differently. Identify the observable pattern before arguing about the label. Irregular forms need lexical checking: written is a participle; wrote is a past-tense form.
A split infinitive is not inherently ungrammatical. Register, rhythm, scope and a specified editorial style may affect which adverb position is preferred.

mistakes.problem: The report appears to have been wrote.
mistakes.repair: The report appears to have been written.
mistakes.reason: The perfect passive chain ends in the lexical past participle written.

mistakes.problem: The clerk enjoys to reading the files.
mistakes.repair: The clerk enjoys reading the files.
mistakes.reason: Enjoy selects an -ing complement in this intended activity sense; do not combine to-infinitival and -ing marking mechanically.

glossary.definition: A clause built around a non-finite verb, interpreted within a larger linguistic or situational context.
glossary.example: To check every signature would take time.

glossary.definition: A modern umbrella label for verbal -ing forms used in several clause functions.
glossary.example: Checking every signature carefully takes time.

glossary.definition: A to-infinitival construction with an expression, often an adverb, between to and the plain verb.
glossary.example: They agreed to jointly fund the laboratory.

modules.title: Verb complementation and differences in meaning
modules.definition: Verb complementation concerns the patterns licensed by a particular verb and its sense. An -ing complement and an infinitival complement may be restricted alternatives or may express different meanings.
foundation: Learn a verb together with a complete pattern: avoid handling fragile objects; hope to finish; ask someone to wait. Avoid normally takes an -ing activity complement; hope normally takes a to-infinitive in this use. An object may belong to the pattern: The supervisor persuaded the clerk to wait. Leaving out or inserting a preposition by analogy can change or break the selected construction. To is not always infinitival: in look forward to meeting, to is a preposition followed by an -ing clause, whereas in hope to meet it marks an infinitive.
intermediate: Several verbs allow both forms with an important ordinary contrast. Remember to lock the cabinet concerns remembering a task before performing it; remember locking the cabinet concerns a memory of the locking. Stop to read the notice means pause another activity in order to read; stop reading means cease the reading activity. Try to restart the computer describes an effort; try restarting the computer proposes restarting as a method to see whether it helps. Neither try-pattern alone guarantees success. Go on checking continues checking; go on to check introduces a subsequent activity in an appropriate sequence.
advanced: Perception verbs can license an object plus a bare infinitive or an -ing form: I saw the boat cross the channel; I saw the boat crossing the channel. The first often presents the event as a whole; the second presents a stage in progress. This contrast should not be exaggerated into a rule that the second event definitely failed to finish. Active causative make and let also normally take a bare infinitive: made us wait; let us leave. Passive made normally introduces to: we were made to wait. Help permits both help us carry and help us to carry. These are selected constructions, not exceptions to be erased by a single formula.
expert: Other pairs differ mainly in viewpoint or context: like swimming and like to swim can both be standard, and preferences vary with meaning and variety. Some patterns allow an explicit non-finite subject, while others require interpretation through the surrounding clause. A dictionary entry helps establish the complement frame; it does not remove the need to read the intended sense. When transforming a sentence, preserve participant roles, aspect and whether an event actually happened. Do not turn remembered to send into remembered sending merely because both phrases contain the same lexical verb: the memory relationship and the assumed event sequence have changed.

patterns.meaning: Selected complement patterns for these ordinary senses.
Ceasing the activity contrasts with pausing for a purpose.

examples.analysis: The -ing clause is the selected activity complement of avoided.

examples.sentence: Mina stopped to compare the two maps.
examples.analysis: The infinitive expresses the purpose of pausing another activity.

examples.sentence: The mechanic saw the belt slipping but did not see it break.
examples.analysis: The -ing form presents an unfolding stage; the bare infinitive presents the breaking event as a whole in the negative perception report.

contrasts.a: Rafi remembered to post the invitation.
contrasts.note: Both are grammatical. The first concerns remembering a task; the second concerns recalling the posting event.

exceptions: Do not treat every pair as sharply different in the same way. Like reading and like to read overlap, while stop reading and stop to read usually have a substantial structural and meaning contrast. Help permits an infinitive with or without to.

mistakes.problem: We look forward to meet the new colleagues.
mistakes.repair: We look forward to meeting the new colleagues.
mistakes.reason: To belongs to the prepositional pattern look forward to; the following activity clause uses -ing.

mistakes.problem: The interruption made us to start again.
mistakes.repair: The interruption made us start again.
mistakes.reason: Active causative make normally selects a bare infinitive; passive were made to start has a different pattern.

glossary.definition: The syntactic frame licensed by a particular word and its sense.
glossary.example: Persuade someone to wait requires an object followed by an infinitive.

glossary.definition: An infinitive without infinitival to, licensed in specified constructions.

modules.title: Purpose, participial clauses and meaning-preserving reduction
modules.definition: A non-finite adjunct adds information such as purpose, time, reason or circumstance. Participial and infinitival clauses can make writing economical, provided their interpreted subject and their relationship to the main clause remain clear.
foundation: An infinitive can express purpose: The librarian moved the lamp to illuminate the desk. The purpose is not simply a second completed event; it explains the intended reason for moving the lamp. In order to can make that relation explicit. An -ing adjunct often shares the main subject: Checking the inventory, the librarian found a missing volume. The librarian is understood as the checker. A past-participial adjunct often gives a passive interpretation: Warned about the leak, the librarian moved the books. The librarian receives the warning rather than issuing it.
intermediate: Perfect participial clauses can make earlier completion explicit: Having checked the inventory, the librarian locked the store. A passive perfect is also possible: Having been warned about the leak, she moved the books. The grammatical form helps organise time and voice, but the exact logical link often comes from context. Warned about the leak may express background, reason or a concessive relation in a suitable sentence; do not translate every participial clause automatically as because. A reduced relative also needs its own interpretation: the letters written yesterday has a passive relation between letters and write, while the researcher writing today presents the researcher as the writer.
advanced: A dangling adjunct arises when the understood participant is missing or misleadingly attached under the intended reading: Having inspected the roof, the leak was obvious does not clearly express who inspected it. If Samir inspected the roof, write After Samir inspected the roof, the leak was obvious to him. Replacing the main clause with Samir found the leak obvious is another valid repair. A passive main clause is not automatically incompatible with an opening participle: Warned about the leak, the tenants were evacuated is coherent because the tenants received the warning. State the intended actor before diagnosing an error.
expert: Not every opening non-finite expression shares the main subject. Absolute constructions have their own subject, as in The checks completed, the team left. Comment expressions such as strictly speaking relate to the speaker’s assessment rather than an ordinary main-clause agent. Purpose clauses can also have implicit agents recoverable in context, especially with passive main clauses; clarity, not an unconditional ban, guides editing. Reduction may remove tense, modality or emphasis: the forms that must be checked cannot simply become the forms checked without losing necessity. A sound transformation therefore compares what each version actually commits the writer to, including the role of every participant and every qualification.

patterns.meaning: A perfect -ing adjunct can make prior completion explicit.
Often a reduced passive relative, subject to lexical meaning and context.

examples.sentence: The clerk opened the window to cool the room.
examples.analysis: The infinitive states an intended purpose; it does not guarantee that the room cooled.

examples.sentence: Having compared both estimates, Samir requested a third.
examples.analysis: Samir is understood as the person who compared the estimates.

examples.sentence: The folders damaged in the flood were photographed before disposal.
examples.analysis: Damaged in the flood modifies folders with a passive interpretation; it does not make folders the agents of damage.

contrasts.a: Warned about the closure, the visitors changed their route.
contrasts.b: Having warned the visitors about the closure, the guide changed the route.
contrasts.note: Both are grammatical. The first has a passive interpretation for the visitors; the second makes the guide the warning agent.

exceptions: An absolute such as Weather permitting, we will inspect the site has an explicit subject inside the opening clause. A comment expression such as frankly speaking is not evaluated by blindly assigning its speaking to the next noun.

mistakes.problem: Having checked the lock, the key was returned to Amina; Amina performed the checking.
mistakes.repair: After Amina checked the lock, the key was returned to her.
mistakes.reason: An explicit finite subject repairs the intended actor relation without claiming that the key checked the lock.

mistakes.problem: The documents that must be signed tomorrow are ready. Proposed equivalent: The documents signed tomorrow are ready.
mistakes.repair: The documents that must be signed tomorrow are ready.
mistakes.reason: The proposed reduction drops the original obligation. Retain the finite relative, or use a carefully qualified alternative that preserves must.

glossary.definition: An adjunct whose intended participant is not clearly or appropriately supplied by the surrounding construction.
glossary.example: Having read the draft, the mistake was obvious leaves the reader unclear.

glossary.definition: A supplementary clause with its own expressed subject.
glossary.example: The doors secured, the guards began their patrol.

modules.title: Control, raising and the interpretation of non-finite subjects
modules.definition: Interpreting a non-finite clause often requires identifying its expressed or understood subject. Control and raising are analytical labels for important differences between constructions; their formal treatment varies between grammatical theories.
foundation: Ask who is understood to perform the action. In Amina tried to unlock the cabinet, Amina is the person trying and the intended unlocker. In Amina persuaded Omar to unlock the cabinet, Omar is the intended unlocker, while Amina is the persuader. These are ordinary subject-control and object-control examples in traditional terminology. The first noun in the sentence does not control every following infinitive, and the nearest noun is not a universal answer either. Learn the selecting verb’s pattern and read the whole context before interpreting the missing participant.
intermediate: Some infinitives express their own subject: It would be useful for Omar to attend identifies Omar as the attendee. Others allow a general or contextual subject: To leave now would be unwise may concern us, another salient group, or people in general, depending on context. With a control verb, participant roles can remain stable under a main-clause passive: Amina persuaded Omar to attend; Omar was persuaded by Amina to attend. Omar is still understood as the attendee. The surface object/subject position changes, so a role-based explanation is more reliable than an instruction to select whichever noun appears immediately before to.
advanced: Raising constructions behave differently. In The parcel seems to have arrived, the parcel is the understood subject of arrive, but seem does not describe an action performed by the parcel. Compare It seems that the parcel has arrived. Dummy there supplies a useful diagnostic: There seems to be a problem is grammatical even though there names no person who seems. A normal agentive control construction such as try does not simply accept dummy there in that way. The contrast concerns the intended dummy interpretation, not every possible use of the word there, which can also be an ordinary place expression.
expert: In one established generative account, control involves an unpronounced subject conventionally written PRO, whose interpretation is supplied by a controller or context. Raising instead relates the visible subject to a position associated with the lower predicate; seem does not assign it the additional participant role that try assigns its subject. These are theoretical analyses, not observable extra words to insert into finished prose, and other frameworks describe the dependency differently. Diagnostics should be used together with meaning and lexical selection, not as one automatic test for every adjective or verb. A further pattern illustrates the limits of a simple subject rule: in The report is easy to read, report is understood as the object of read, whereas in Amina is eager to read, Amina is the understood reader. Such differences make careful syntactic analysis useful, but a beginner can begin by asking who does what and which complement pattern is licensed.

patterns.meaning: A standard subject-control example: the subject is also the intended performer in the complement.

patterns.form: There + seem + to be + noun phrase
patterns.meaning: An established raising pattern with dummy there.

examples.sentence: Nora tried to repair the hinge.
examples.analysis: Nora is both the person trying and the intended repairer.

examples.sentence: Nora persuaded Imran to repair the hinge.
examples.analysis: Imran is understood as the repairer; Nora is the persuader.

examples.sentence: There seem to be several errors in the total.
examples.analysis: Dummy there has no semantic agent role; the plural associate supports seem in this careful formal version.

contrasts.a: The courier tried to arrive early.
contrasts.b: The courier seems to have arrived early.
contrasts.note: Both are grammatical. Try attributes an effort to the courier; seem presents an appearance or inference about the arrival without attributing an act of seeming to the courier.

exceptions: The subject of an infinitive can be explicit after for, contextually understood, controlled by a main-clause participant, or involved in another dependency. Do not teach that every infinitive has the subject of its nearest finite clause.

mistakes.problem: Amina persuaded Omar to leave. Analysis: Amina must be the leaver because she is the sentence’s subject.
mistakes.repair: Amina persuaded Omar to leave. In the ordinary intended reading, Omar is the leaver.
mistakes.reason: Persuade licenses object/goal control; the matrix subject is the persuader.

mistakes.problem: There seems to be a delay. Correction proposed: A person must replace there because every infinitive needs a human subject.
mistakes.repair: No correction is needed: There seems to be a delay.
mistakes.reason: The established dummy-there raising construction does not require a human agent.

glossary.definition: A dependency in which a participant or the context supplies the interpretation of a non-finite clause’s unexpressed subject.
glossary.example: Rafi tried to wait makes Rafi the intended waiter.

glossary.definition: An analytical label for constructions such as seem, where the visible subject is interpreted with the lower predicate without an additional participant role from the raising predicate.
glossary.example: The parcel seems to have arrived.

glossary.definition: A notation for an unpronounced subject in a traditional generative analysis of control.
glossary.example: An analysis may represent Rafi tried [PRO to wait].

questions.prompt: In The archivist hopes to finish today, which expression is the non-finite complement?
options: hopes
to finish today
today alone
The archivist
questions.why: To finish today is an infinitival clause complement. Hopes is the finite matrix verb; today alone is only an adverbial expression.

questions.prompt: Complete the perfect passive infinitive: The letter appears to have been ____.
options: written
writing
write
wrote
questions.why: Have been written is a perfect passive chain ending in the lexical participle written.

questions.prompt: Which analysis distinguishes a verbal -ing clause from a noun phrase?
options: Carefully is an adjective modifying a noun in reading the files carefully.
Reading the files carefully contains a verbal reading with an object and adverb.
The careful reading of the files must contain a finite verb.
Every spelling ending in -ing is automatically a verb.
questions.why: The direct object the files and adverb carefully support a verbal analysis. A noun reading instead permits determiner/adjective and an of-phrase.

questions.prompt: We look forward to ____ the new curator.
options: meet
meeting
met
meets
questions.why: In look forward to, to is prepositional and the following activity complement uses -ing.

questions.prompt: Mina stopped to read the notice. What does the infinitive normally express?
options: Proof that the notice was never read
A past passive event
The ending of the reading activity
The purpose of pausing another activity
questions.why: Stopped to read normally means paused in order to read; stopped reading would mean ceased reading.

questions.prompt: Review: They helped us to carry the boxes.
options: Helped must always be followed by an -ing form.
To must be removed because help never allows it.
Us must be replaced by we.
No error: help permits an infinitive with or without to.
questions.why: Help us carry and help us to carry are both standard; the object pronoun us is appropriate.

questions.prompt: The intended inspector is Samir. Which revision clearly supplies that participant?
options: After the roof inspected Samir, the leak was obvious.
Having inspected the roof, the leak was obvious.
After Samir inspected the roof, the leak was obvious to him.
Having inspected the roof, the leak inspected Samir.
questions.why: The finite after-clause explicitly identifies Samir as inspector while preserving that he found the leak obvious.

questions.prompt: Which opening clause has its own expressed subject rather than an ordinary shared main-clause subject?
options: Weather permitting, Nora will visit.
Warned about the closure, Nora stayed.
Having checked the list, Nora called.
To check the list, Nora stayed.
questions.why: Weather permitting is an absolute construction with weather as its own subject. The other examples have an understood participant linked to Nora.

questions.prompt: In Amina persuaded Omar to attend, who is the understood attendee in the ordinary intended reading?
options: No participant can be inferred
Amina only
Omar
Both must attend
questions.why: Persuade licenses object/goal control: Omar is the intended attendee, while Amina is the persuader.

questions.prompt: Which example supports a raising analysis of seem rather than an agentive subject-control analysis?
options: There seems to be a delay.
The technician tried to restart the machine.
The supervisor persuaded us to stay.
The guide asked us to wait.
questions.why: Dummy there can occur with seems to be without naming an agent of seem. Try, persuade and ask in the other examples involve participant/control relationships.

questions.prompt: Classify the verb forms in We may have been waiting too long. Identify the finite item.
questions.model: May is the finite modal. Have is a plain form selected by may, been is a participle selected by perfect have, and waiting is the -ing form selected by progressive be.
rubric: Identify may rather than waiting as finite.
Explain the auxiliary selection order.
alternatives: Other answers are acceptable if they preserve the stated meaning and meet the listed structural requirements.

questions.prompt: Identify the function of Checking the details in Checking the details takes time.
questions.model: The whole non-finite -ing clause Checking the details functions as the subject of takes.
rubric: Identify the whole clause, not only checking.
Keep its subject function separate from the verbal category of checking.
alternatives: Other answers are acceptable if they preserve the stated meaning and meet the listed structural requirements.

questions.prompt: Complete with the required participles: The document is believed to have been ____(write), and the witness denies having ____(see) it.
rubric: Use the past participle written in the perfect passive infinitive.
Use seen after perfect having.
alternatives: Other answers are acceptable if they preserve the stated meaning and meet the listed structural requirements.

questions.prompt: Explain the category difference between the careful examination of the files and examining the files carefully.
questions.model: Examination is a noun head with adjective careful and an of-phrase. Examining is a verb heading a non-finite clause, taking the files as object and carefully as adverbial modifier.
rubric: Compare observable structure, not just translation.
Do not call examining finite merely because it has an object.
alternatives: Other answers are acceptable if they preserve the stated meaning and meet the listed structural requirements.

questions.prompt: Explain a normal meaning contrast between I remembered to close the window and I remembered closing the window.
questions.model: The first concerns remembering the task before closing; the second concerns recalling the closing event.
rubric: Identify the different memory relationships.
Do not present the sentences as automatically interchangeable.
alternatives: Other answers are acceptable if they preserve the stated meaning and meet the listed structural requirements.

questions.prompt: Explain try to restart the system versus try restarting the system.
questions.model: Try to restart describes an effort to achieve restarting. Try restarting proposes restarting as an experimental method that may help. Neither wording alone guarantees success.
rubric: Distinguish effort from a proposed method.
Do not invent a successful outcome.
alternatives: Other answers are acceptable if they preserve the stated meaning and meet the listed structural requirements.

questions.prompt: Reconstruct using each supplied unit once: to finish the survey / the researcher / hoped.
questions.model: The researcher hoped to finish the survey.
rubric: Use hoped as the finite matrix verb.
Keep the supplied infinitival complement intact without adding a new participant.
alternatives: Other answers are acceptable if they preserve the stated meaning and meet the listed structural requirements.

questions.prompt: Why does seeing The pilot saw the kite falling not prove that the kite never reached the ground?
questions.model: The -ing complement presents an unfolding stage of the event. It does not by itself state that the event failed to continue to completion.
rubric: Explain the viewpoint of falling.
Separate what is presented from an unsupported later outcome.
alternatives: Other answers are acceptable if they preserve the stated meaning and meet the listed structural requirements.

questions.prompt: Combine faithfully: Amina checked the seals. After that, Amina opened the container. Use a perfect -ing opening.
questions.model: Having checked the seals, Amina opened the container.
rubric: Keep Amina as checker and opener.
Use having checked to preserve the explicit earlier completion.
alternatives: Other answers are acceptable if they preserve the stated meaning and meet the listed structural requirements.

questions.prompt: Expand without changing the warning recipient: Warned about the leak, the tenants were evacuated.
questions.model: The tenants had been warned about the leak. They were then evacuated.
rubric: Keep the tenants as recipients of the warning.
Retain the evacuation rather than making the tenants its organisers.
alternatives: The tenants had received a warning about the leak. They were subsequently evacuated.

questions.prompt: Why is replacing the forms that must be signed with the forms signed an unreliable meaning-preserving reduction?
questions.model: The finite relative expresses necessity through must. The past-participial modifier does not retain that obligation and may instead suggest completed signing.
rubric: Identify the lost modal meaning.
Explain why brevity alone does not justify the change.
alternatives: Other answers are acceptable if they preserve the stated meaning and meet the listed structural requirements.

questions.prompt: Analyse Weather permitting, we will inspect the site: identify the opening clause’s subject.
questions.model: Weather is the expressed subject of the absolute permitting clause; it is not an activity performed by we.
rubric: Identify the internal subject weather.
Avoid applying an unconditional shared-main-subject rule.
alternatives: Other answers are acceptable if they preserve the stated meaning and meet the listed structural requirements.

questions.prompt: Compare Nora tried to repair the hinge with Nora seems to have repaired the hinge.
questions.model: The first attributes an effort to Nora, who is also the intended repairer. The second presents an appearance or inference about Nora’s repair; seem does not assign Nora an additional agent role.
rubric: Separate an effort from an attributed appearance/inference.
Do not turn seems into proof that the repair succeeded.
alternatives: Other answers are acceptable if they preserve the stated meaning and meet the listed structural requirements.

questions.prompt: Identify the attendee in Omar was persuaded by Amina to attend. Does the passive change that understood role?
questions.model: Omar is the understood attendee. The passive changes his surface main-clause position from object in Amina persuaded Omar to subject, while preserving that role.
rubric: Retain Omar as attendee.
Distinguish grammatical position from the relevant participant relationship.
alternatives: Other answers are acceptable if they preserve the stated meaning and meet the listed structural requirements.

questions.prompt: Explain why To leave now would be unwise does not identify one named leaver without context.
questions.model: The infinitive has no expressed subject. Context may supply us, another salient group or a general human interpretation.
rubric: Recognise contextual/arbitrary interpretation.
Do not invent a named actor from the sentence alone.
alternatives: Other answers are acceptable if they preserve the stated meaning and meet the listed structural requirements.

questions.prompt: Compare the relation of report to read in The report is easy to read with Amina to read in Amina is eager to read.
questions.model: Report is understood as the object of read; Amina is understood as the reader/subject in the eager construction.
rubric: Identify the two different gaps or participant relationships.
Do not classify every adjective-plus-infinitive pattern by one subject-sharing rule.
alternatives: Other answers are acceptable if they preserve the stated meaning and meet the listed structural requirements.

questions.prompt: Repair the analysis rather than the grammatical sentence: There seems to be a delay. There must name the person who performs seeming, and be is past tense.
questions.model: There is a dummy element in an established raising construction, not a person or an agent of seeming. Be is an infinitival plain form after to, not a past-tense verb.
rubric: Keep the original grammatical sentence.
Correct both the agent claim and the verb-form claim.
alternatives: Other answers are acceptable if they preserve the stated meaning and meet the listed structural requirements.

questions.prompt: Write one sentence with stop + -ing and one with stop + to-infinitive. Explain the intended difference.
questions.model: I stopped checking the stock at six. / I stopped to check the stock before leaving. The first ends the checking activity; the second pauses another activity for checking.
rubric: Use both selected constructions accurately.
Explain the difference without asserting that all stopping events have the same purpose.
alternatives: Other answers are acceptable if they preserve the stated meaning and meet the listed structural requirements.

questions.prompt: Compare The team decided to immediately suspend the trial with The team immediately decided to suspend the trial. Must the first be corrected? What possible timing difference matters?
questions.model: The split infinitive in the first is grammatical. Immediately clearly modifies suspension there; in the second it can modify the decision. Revise only if clarity or a stated style requirement calls for it, preserving the intended timing.
rubric: Reject an absolute grammatical ban on split infinitives.
Explain the possible difference in adverb attachment and preserve the intended meaning.
alternatives: A context can make both refer to the same timing. A stated house-style preference may justify a clear unsplit rewrite, but does not make all splits ungrammatical.

corrections.prompt: Correct only the genuine problem or faulty analysis: The archive appears to have been destroy last year.
corrections.model: The archive appears to have been destroyed last year.
rubric: Use the lexical past participle destroyed at the end of the perfect passive infinitive.
Retain the attributed appearance and the stated past time.
alternatives: Other answers are acceptable if they preserve the stated meaning and meet the listed structural requirements.

corrections.prompt: Correct only the genuine problem or faulty analysis: She denies having saw the confidential letter.
corrections.model: She denies having seen the confidential letter.
rubric: Use seen after perfect having.
Retain the denial rather than assert that she saw the letter.
alternatives: Other answers are acceptable if they preserve the stated meaning and meet the listed structural requirements.

corrections.prompt: Correct only the genuine problem or faulty analysis: We look forward to hear from the curator.
corrections.model: We look forward to hearing from the curator.
rubric: Recognise prepositional to in look forward to.
Use an -ing complement without changing the expected communication.
alternatives: Other answers are acceptable if they preserve the stated meaning and meet the listed structural requirements.

corrections.prompt: Correct only the genuine problem or faulty analysis: The interruption made us to start again.
corrections.model: The interruption made us start again.
rubric: Use a bare infinitive after active causative make.
Retain us as the intended starters.
alternatives: Other answers are acceptable if they preserve the stated meaning and meet the listed structural requirements.

corrections.prompt: Correct only the genuine problem or faulty analysis: They helped us to carry the records.
corrections.model: No change is required. They helped us to carry the records.
rubric: Accept standard help with to.
Do not introduce an error merely because the version without to is also possible.
alternatives: Other answers are acceptable if they preserve the stated meaning and meet the listed structural requirements.

corrections.prompt: Revise for unambiguous formal reference, explicitly naming the stated checker: Having checked the labels, the boxes were delivered to Samir. Intended: Samir checked the labels before receiving the boxes.
corrections.model: After Samir checked the labels, the boxes were delivered to him.
rubric: Give the checking its intended subject Samir.
Preserve that the boxes were delivered to Samir; do not make him the deliverer.
alternatives: Other answers are acceptable if they preserve the stated meaning and meet the listed structural requirements.

corrections.prompt: Correct only the genuine problem or faulty analysis: The papers which must be reviewed tomorrow are ready. Proposed shorter equivalent: The papers reviewed tomorrow are ready.
corrections.model: Keep the original: The papers which must be reviewed tomorrow are ready.
rubric: Recognise that the original is grammatical.
Reject the proposed equivalence because it drops must, not because all reduced relatives are wrong.
alternatives: Other answers are acceptable if they preserve the stated meaning and meet the listed structural requirements.

corrections.prompt: Correct only the genuine problem or faulty analysis: Amina persuaded Omar to wait. Analysis: Amina is necessarily the waiter because she is the matrix subject.
corrections.model: The sentence needs no correction. In the ordinary intended reading, Omar is the waiter and Amina is the persuader.
rubric: Correct the analysis rather than the sentence.
Identify object/goal control without replacing the stated participants.
alternatives: Other answers are acceptable if they preserve the stated meaning and meet the listed structural requirements.

transformations.prompt: Rewrite using a perfect passive infinitive without strengthening the evidence: It appears that the records were moved before the inspection.
transformations.model: The records appear to have been moved before the inspection.
rubric: Preserve appears rather than asserting confirmed movement.
Use to have been moved and retain before the inspection.
alternatives: Other answers are acceptable if they preserve the stated meaning and meet the listed structural requirements.

transformations.prompt: Use a perfect participial opening and retain the named checker: After Nora had compared both estimates, she requested a third.
transformations.model: Having compared both estimates, Nora requested a third.
rubric: Keep Nora as comparer and requester.
Preserve earlier completed comparison with having compared.
alternatives: Other answers are acceptable if they preserve the stated meaning and meet the listed structural requirements.

writing.prompt: Write a 100–140-word archive update containing an -ing complement after a selecting verb, a purpose infinitive, a past-participial noun modifier and a perfect participial opening. Identify their understood participants and distinguish a reported appearance from a confirmed fact.
writing.model:
Samir has begun checking the condition of the archived maps. He avoids touching fragile edges and uses a support board to protect each sheet. The labels printed on Monday identify the collection but do not give the date of every map. Having compared the old register with the new list, Samir has found three entries that need clarification. He plans to ask the curator for advice before changing them. The maps appear to have been moved during an earlier repair, although that history has not yet been confirmed. Samir will record the uncertainty rather than silently invent missing dates. His next task is to photograph the labels and attach the images to the catalogue.

Analysis: Avoids touching selects an -ing complement. To protect each sheet states Samir’s intended purpose. Printed on Monday modifies labels with a passive interpretation. Having compared has Samir as its understood subject. Appear to have been moved attributes earlier movement without treating it as confirmed.
rubric: Produce 100–140 words of original update prose before any grammatical annotation.
Include and identify all four specified non-finite patterns.
Keep the checker, protector and recipients clear; do not introduce a dangling participant.
Preserve uncertainty in any reporting or raising construction.
alternatives: Other answers are acceptable if they preserve the stated meaning and meet the listed structural requirements.

recall.prompt: Recall Day 5: In The curator has been checking the inventory, which item is finite and what forms follow it?
recall.model: Has is finite; been is a participle selected by perfect have, and checking is an -ing form selected by progressive be.
rubric: Identify the finite auxiliary.
Explain the selection chain rather than calling every item finite.
alternatives: Other answers are acceptable if they preserve the stated meaning and meet the listed structural requirements.

recall.prompt: Recall Day 17: Why is may have been checking not may has been checking?
recall.model: A core modal selects the plain form have, even with a singular subject. Finite agreement is not added to have after may.
rubric: Identify the modal’s form requirement.
Do not make every verb in an auxiliary chain agree independently.
alternatives: Other answers are acceptable if they preserve the stated meaning and meet the listed structural requirements.

recall.prompt: Recall Day 19: Compare Nora had repaired the scanner and Nora had the scanner repaired.
recall.model: The first is a past-perfect construction describing Nora’s repair in the ordinary reading. The second normally says Nora arranged the repair, with someone else performing it.
rubric: Distinguish auxiliary perfect have from causative have.
Preserve the different participant interpretations.
alternatives: Other answers are acceptable if they preserve the stated meaning and meet the listed structural requirements.

checklist: I identify verb form and grammatical function separately.
I check a verb’s selected complement pattern and explain meaning differences.
I preserve participants, modality and time when shortening clauses.
I distinguish genuine dangling structures from coherent passive or absolute constructions.
I use control/raising labels as explanations of specific patterns, not universal shortcuts.
